name: Tensor Memory (TMEM): a third accumulator store, between registers and shared memory
arithmetic_intensity: TMEM changes the capacity budget of a GEMM or attention mainloop rather than the roofline. It is a dedicated on-chip scratchpad wired into the tensor cores, with structure and rules that come straight from the PTX ISA: on sm_100a/sm_100f it is a two-dimensional matrix of 512 columns and 128 lanes per CTA with 32-bit cells, addressed by a 32-bit value whose high 16 bits are the lane and low 16 bits the column; allocation is dynamic, performed by a SINGLE WARP in the CTA, in units of 32 columns with a power-of-2 column count, and every allocation must be deallocated before the kernel exits. The arithmetic consequence is about pipelining depth rather than bytes: because MMA accumulators and operands can live in TMEM instead of registers, a kernel can keep several MMAs in flight and run elementwise work on the CUDA cores concurrently. FA-4's backward pass is the concrete example - it stores S and P in TMEM in stages (S and P share one column set, dP/dS/dQ share another, because five full accumulators do not fit), stores transposed intermediates directly in TMEM in the exact operand-A layout the dV and dK MMAs consume (removing a shared-memory round trip), and notes tcgen05.mma can source operand A from TMEM.
scales_with: TMEM column budget per CTA (512 on sm_100a, extended to 576 per CUTLASS's Blackwell/Rubin entries)
number of MMAs kept in flight
CTA group size (2-CTA MMA spans both CTAs' TMEM)
workarounds: Budget TMEM columns explicitly per pipeline stage and reuse columns across stages
Let one warp own all TMEM allocation/deallocation so the allocation is serialized and correct
Store transposed intermediates in TMEM in operand-A layout to skip a shared-memory round trip
Use TMEM-resident accumulators to keep several MMAs in flight while CUDA cores do elementwise work
notes: This record exists because TMEM is the specific hardware reason a Blackwell kernel looks structurally different from a Hopper kernel, and because it is what makes shared-memory traffic - not FLOPs - the backward-pass bottleneck on B200 (per FA-4's feeds-and-speeds: backward needs 3328 SMEM cycles per tile versus 2560 tensor-core cycles). TMEM does not exist on Hopper; the closest Hopper analogue is keeping accumulators in shared memory, which is what wgmma's D-in-shared-memory mode allows and why Hopper register pressure is the binding constraint there. CUTLASS README lists 'Extended TMEM size from 512 COL to 576 COL' among the SM107/Rubin entries, and the FlashMLA build explicitly fails on register spilling - a reminder that both stores are finite.
